en.headline: WhatsApp hijacking scams jump 170 per cent in first seven months
en.dek: Police recorded 1,993 WhatsApp account-takeover cases from January to July, with losses of HK$146 million, and said phishing texts remain the main entry point.
body: Police said they recorded 1,993 WhatsApp account-hijacking cases in the first seven months of 2026, up 169.7 per cent from 739 in the same period last year and already higher than the 1,669 cases logged in the whole of 2025. Combined losses came to about HK$146.3 million, down 22.7 per cent year on year.

The cases made up 99 per cent of 2,020 instant-messaging account hijacks in the period. Superintendent Hui Yee-wai of the Cyber Security and Technology Crime Bureau said overall technology crime had fallen, but messaging hijacks had risen because WhatsApp is widely used and because artificial intelligence has made fake websites easier to produce.

Chief Inspector Alvin Wong said most attacks still begin with a phishing text that claims an account will be frozen unless the recipient clicks a link. After taking over an account, scammers often study chats before impersonating relatives, colleagues, estate agents or lawyers and asking for urgent transfers. Police cited a property buyer who lost about HK$1.17 million and an investment-firm finance manager who transferred HK$12.2 million after instructions from a hijacked supervisor account.

Officers advised the public not to tap unexpected links, to confirm any payment request on a separate channel such as a phone call, and to check the receiving account name before transferring money. The force pointed people to the Scameter tool and the anti-scam hotline 18222.

zh.headline: 首七個月WhatsApp騎劫騙案升近一倍七 損失1.46億
zh.dek: 警方錄得1,993宗WhatsApp帳戶被騎劫個案，損失約1.46億元，指大部分仍由釣魚短訊入手。
body: 警方表示，今年1至7月錄得1,993宗WhatsApp帳戶騎劫騙案，較去年同期739宗升169.7%，已超2025年全年的1,669宗。損失金額約1.463億元，按年跌22.7%。
同期即時通訊軟件帳戶騎劫案共2,020宗，WhatsApp佉99%。網絡安全及科技罪案調查科警司許綮惠表示，整體科技罪案有所下跌，但通訊軟件騎劫案上升，與市民廣泛使用WhatsApp，以及人工智能令假網站更易製作有關。
高級警司黃長興指，大部分案件仍由釣魚短訊開始，內容聲稱帳戶即將被凍結，誘使事主點擊連結。騎劫成功後，騙徒會先翻查對話，再假冒親友、同事、地產經紀或律師要求緊急轉帳。警方舉例，一名準買家損失約117萬元；另有投資公司財務經理按被騎劫上司帳戶的指示轉帳1,220萬元。
警方呼籲市民勿隨意點擊不明連結，如收到付款或轉帳要求，應改用電話等另一渠道核實對方身份，轉帳前核對收款帳戶名稱，亦可使用「防騙視伏器」或致18222防騙熱線。
